cards.headline: One dead, 50 evacuated after fire at Jurong East HDB flat
bullets: One person died and 50 people were evacuated after a fire at a Jurong East HDB flat.
The fire started early on August 16 and smoke was seen coming from a third-floor unit.
Firefighters found an unresponsive person in the living room who was later pronounced dead.
This is the fourth fatal HDB flat fire reported since late July.

cards.headline: NTU retrofits building to prevent fatal bird collisions
bullets: NTU's Art, Design and Media building now has anti-collision decals on its glass panels.
The decals aim to stop birds from crashing into the building.
Student efforts and NTU funding covered the $119,000 cost for the project.
The decals are expected to last about seven years and are nearly invisible.

cards.headline: Former PHV driver-turned-vending machine boss now broke; investors worry about their $4m
bullets: A former private-hire car driver was declared bankrupt on July 14.
He convinced over 40 investors to put in $4 million for his vending machine business.
Investors are now worried about getting their money back after returns stopped.
Police are investigating after receiving multiple reports from the investors.

cards.headline: Sheltered linkway to connect Tanjong Pagar CC to MRT station in a few years’ time
bullets: A new sheltered walkway will link Tanjong Pagar Community Club to the Tanjong Pagar MRT station.
The walkway will cover crossings over four roads, making walking safer and easier.
It will connect residents to both Tanjong Pagar and Cantonment MRT stations when completed.
A new youth hub with gaming and study areas will also open in the area.

cards.headline: Driver taken to hospital following accident in Geylang involving 5 cars, motorcycle
bullets: A 67-year-old driver was taken to hospital after six vehicles crashed in Geylang.
The accident involved five cars and one motorcycle.
It happened on Geylang East Central near Sims Drive.
The crash blocked all lanes and caused road closures.

cards.headline: How Singapore’s Ascott grew from its first serviced residence into a global hospitality business
bullets: Ascott started in 1984 with Singapore's first international serviced residence.
Today, Ascott has over 1,000 properties in more than 40 countries.
The company focuses on giving guests space and flexibility to live, not just stay.
Ascott uses Singapore as a testbed for new hospitality ideas.
Travellers now want to feel connected to a place, not just visit it.

cards.headline: Thailand beat Singapore 3-1 in first leg of ASEAN football championship semi-finals
bullets: Thailand beat Singapore 3-1 in the first leg of their football championship semi-final.
Thai striker Teerasak Poeiphimai scored two goals in the first half.
Singapore's Ilhan Fandi scored one goal to reduce the deficit.
Thailand has won their last 11 matches against Singapore.

cards.headline: Marriage, parenthood workgroup advances early proposals to not 'lose time' on falling birth rates: Indranee
bullets: Government plans to help families will be announced soon, starting with the National Day Rally.
Early proposals focus on the cost of raising kids and childcare support.
More measures to support marriage and parenthood are coming after the initial announcements.
Workplace culture changes to help parents will take more time to figure out.

cards.headline: Singapore women's netball team retain Asian Championship crown
bullets: Singapore's netball team beat Hong Kong 57-33 to keep their Asian Championship title.
This is the fifth time the Singapore Vandas have won the tournament.
The team also qualified for next year's Netball World Cup in Sydney.

cards.headline: NEA rebuts accusations of misappropriation, corruption over Beverage Container Return Scheme refunds
bullets: NEA says over $550,000 has been refunded for 5.5 million drink containers returned.
The agency explained one return machine visit can handle multiple containers.
This clarifies claims of money being lost or misused in the deposit scheme.
The Beverage Container Return Scheme has had over one million successful transactions.

cards.headline: UK housebuilders plagued by upheaval as Burnham hopes for homes
bullets: UK housebuilders' profits have dropped by half since 2022.
Rising building costs and higher mortgage rates are hurting sales.
Some firms are building and selling fewer homes to save money.
Government support for first-time buyers ended in 2022, making it harder to buy.
Complex planning rules are also a major obstacle for developers.

cards.headline: Citi’s Singapore country officer Lee Lung-Nien elected Singapore Golf Association president
bullets: Lee Lung-Nien, Citi's Singapore boss, is the new president of the Singapore Golf Association.
He was elected at the association's annual meeting on Friday.
This is the first time in 65 years the golf president role was contested.
Lee will serve a four-year term leading the SGA.

cards.headline: 2026 Mercedes-Benz GLB review: 95 reasons you’ll know it’s a Mercedes
bullets: The new Mercedes-Benz GLB electric car has 95 stars on its front grille.
It can help you find the nearest nasi lemak, but the best is in Malaysia.
The GLB 200 electric costs S$290,888 and has a range of 453 km.
The pricier GLB 250+ electric costs S$325,888, offers 674 km range and has fancy massage seats.
The car's app can find over 7,000 charging points in Singapore.

cards.headline: OpenAI steps up Singapore footprint, in talks to lease 100,000 sq ft in Shaw Tower
bullets: OpenAI is talking about renting 100,000 sq ft of office space at Shaw Tower.
This space would cover five floors in the new 32-storey building.
AI companies are expanding into Singapore, with OpenAI being the latest.

cards.headline: Reflections from The Open: Shaping the future of golf in Singapore and the region
bullets: Singapore Golf Association looks to The Open for ideas on growing the game.
The Open championship is a platform for innovation and collaboration in golf.
Top golfers' success shows the importance of preparation and resilience.
Singapore golfers Shannon Tan and Justin Kuk are showing good results.
The Singapore Open offers a chance for local players to compete in major championships.

cards.headline: Karang guni man, 59, steals S$2,000 sugarcane juicer at Redhill Food Centre, sells it for about S$20
bullets: A man stole a S$2,000 sugarcane juicer and sold it for S$20.
The 59-year-old was fined S$2,500 for the theft.
He could go to jail for a week if he can't pay the fine.
The juicer was taken from Redhill Food Centre while waiting to be returned.

cards.headline: NUS professor, 47, becomes own test subject in longevity study, cuts biological age to 32
bullets: NUS professor's biological age dropped to 32 from 47 after a lifestyle study.
He fasted for 20 hours daily and exercised for 90 minutes each morning.
His diet focused on leafy greens, lean protein, and healthy fats.
His resting heart rate improved significantly, and sleep quality increased.
He also lost over 18kg during the experiment.

cards.headline: S'porean man, 36, sets childhood friend on fire, stabs girlfriend while out on bail, jailed 1 year
bullets: A man was jailed one year for setting his friend on fire and attacking his girlfriend.
He fled Singapore for five years after the fire incident.
While on bail for the fire, he punched and stabbed his girlfriend.
The friend he set on fire suffered burns needing multiple operations.

cards.headline: 12 Best Water Bottles In Singapore For On-The-Go Hydration, Including Insulated & Glass Ones
bullets: The LARQ Self-Cleaning Bottle uses UV light to kill 99% of bacteria.
Some bottles can keep drinks cold for up to 40 hours.
Foldable bottles like the Vapur Anti-Bottle save space in bags.
Smart bottles can remind you to drink water and track intake.
New water bottles offer features like built-in cups and self-cleaning tech.

cards.headline: 8 Schools In SG That Have Been Revamped To Lifestyle Hubs, Arts Centres & Newer Schools
bullets: Former Nan Chiau High School is now New Bahru, a lifestyle and creative hub with cafes and workshops.
Old School at Mount Sophia, once Methodist Girls' School, became an arts hub before redevelopment.
The Olson Building, a former MGS structure, is now a clubhouse for Sophia Hills condominium.
The old Serangoon Garden South School campus will be a new lifestyle hub with fitness and community spaces.
Goodman Arts Centre, built on Tun Seri Lanang Secondary School grounds, hosts galleries and studios.
